title: Female Prime Minister: Shangguan Wan'er
synopsis: Shangguan Wan'er, known as China's "female prime minister" was a trusted aid of Wu Zetian, the first and only woman emperor of China.

fullText.simplified:
“巾帼宰相”——上官婉儿

    唐朝的武则天是中国历史上唯一的女皇帝，她的出现不仅开创了历史先河，而且引领了女性参政的热潮。在她退位后的八九年时间内，相继出现了数名杰出的女政治家，人们将这段空前绝后的历史称为“红妆时代”。上官婉儿作为武则天的第一助手，是红妆时代的重要代表人物之一。
    上官婉儿出生在一个政治世家，爷爷是宰相。但在她出生后不久，爷爷和父亲因为反对当时还是皇后的武则天而被武则天所杀，她和妈妈被罚入宫成了低等宫女。在做宫女的期间，上官婉儿坚持学习，因才华出众而小有名气。等到上官婉儿十三岁时，武则天听说宫里有个这样优秀的宫女，便把上官婉儿叫到了自己面前。武则天问了很多问题，上官婉儿对答如流。武则天十分爱惜人才，虽然上官婉儿的爷爷和父亲反对过自己，但武则天并没有因此不信任上官婉儿。她向上官婉儿表达了诚意并邀请她协助自己治理国家。上官婉儿被感化，放下个人恩怨，成为了武则天的助手，从此走上了从政之路。
    在之后的二十多年里，上官婉儿一直陪伴在武则天身边。她得到了武则天的重用，出色地处理了许多国家大事，充分地展现了个人智慧和政治才能。她被人们称为“巾帼宰相”，意思是说她虽然是女子，却能像男子一样担当重任，参与国家大事。武则天退位后，上官婉儿继续得到了下一任皇帝的信任，仍然拥有参与国家大事决策的权力。此外，她还劝说新皇帝设立学馆，为优秀的人才提供学习和施展才华的场所，大力开展文化活动，为国家培养了一大批优秀的人才。同时她本人还写下了许多优美的诗文，不但受到人们的赞赏，还成为当时全国诗人学习的榜样，在历史上留下了“才女”的美名。
    上官婉儿的生命止步在47岁。那一年新皇帝突然病死，国家发生政变。乱军冲进皇宫，上官婉儿被杀。后世史书对上官婉儿的生平进行了评述，虽然肯定了其文学才能和对文化做出的贡献，但也因各种各样的原因，留下了一些污点性的描写。2013年，考古学家发现了上官婉儿的墓，墓碑上一篇900多字的墓志铭成为重要的考古材料。墓志铭由武则天的女儿——也是红妆时代的另一位代表人物，太平公主所写。墓志铭书写了上官婉儿的一生，用极其优美和深刻的词汇赞美了上官婉儿的才华和品格。人们通过这篇墓志铭，认识了一个更全面的上官婉儿。
    但不管是史书的评述，还是墓志铭的描写，真实的上官婉儿是什么样的，也许我们很难完全了解。这正是历史的迷人之处，一个红妆时代的“巾帼宰相”，有着太多有意思的可能。
fullText.traditional:
“巾幗宰相”——上官婉兒

    唐朝的武則天是中國歷史上唯一的女皇帝，她的出現不僅開創了歷史先河，而且引領了女性參政的熱潮。在她退位後的八九年時間內，相繼出現了數名傑出的女政治家，人們將這段空前絕後的歷史稱為“紅妝時代”。上官婉兒作為武則天的第一助手，是紅妝時代的重要代表人物之一。
    上官婉兒出生在一個政治世家，爺爺是宰相。但在她出生後不久，爺爺和父親因為反對當時還是皇后的武則天而被武則天所殺，她和媽媽被罰入宮成了低等宮女。在做宮女的期間，上官婉兒堅持學習，因才華出眾而小有名氣。等到上官婉兒十三歲時，武則天聽說宮裡有個這樣優秀的宮女，便把上官婉兒叫到了自己面前。武則天問了很多問題，上官婉兒對答如流。武則天十分愛惜人才，雖然上官婉兒的爺爺和父親反對過自己，但武則天並沒有因此不信任上官婉兒。她向上官婉兒表達了誠意並邀請她協助自己治理國家。上官婉兒被感化，放下個人恩怨，成為了武則天的助手，從此走上了從政之路。
    在之後的二十多年裡，上官婉兒一直陪伴在武則天身邊。她得到了武則天的重用，出色地處理了許多國家大事，充分地展現了個人智慧和政治才能。她被人們稱為“巾幗宰相”，意思是說她雖然是女子，卻能像男子一樣擔當重任，參與國家大事。武則天退位後，上官婉兒繼續得到了下一任皇帝的信任，仍然擁有參與國家大事決策的權力。此外，她還勸說新皇帝設立學館，為優秀的人才提供學習和施展才華的場所，大力開展文化活動，為國家培養了一大批優秀的人才。同時她本人還寫下了許多優美的詩文，不但受到人們的讚賞，還成為當時全國詩人學習的榜樣，在歷史上留下了“才女”的美名。
    上官婉兒的生命止步在47歲。那一年新皇帝突然病死，國家發生政變。亂軍衝進皇宮，上官婉兒被殺。後世史書對上官婉兒的生平進行了評述，雖然肯定了其文學才能和對文化做出的貢獻，但也因各種各樣的原因，留下了一些污點性的描寫。2013年，考古學家發現了上官婉兒的墓，墓碑上一篇900多字的墓誌銘成為重要的考古材料。墓誌銘由武則天的女兒——也是紅妝時代的另一位代表人物，太平公主所寫。墓誌銘書寫了上官婉兒的一生，用極其優美和深刻的詞彙讚美了上官婉兒的才華和品格。人們通過這篇墓誌銘，認識了一個更全面的上官婉兒。
    但不管是史書的評述，還是墓誌銘的描寫，真實的上官婉兒是什麼樣的，也許我們很難完全了解。這正是歷史的迷人之處，一個紅妝時代的“巾幗宰相”，有著太多有意思的可能。

sentences.traditional: 亂軍衝進皇宮，上官婉兒被殺。
sentences.pinyin: luàn jūn chōng jìn huáng gōng shàng guān wǎn ér bèi shā
sentences.english: That year, the new emperor suddenly died of illness, and a coup occurred in the country.

sentences.simplified: 后世史书对上官婉儿的生平进行了评述，
sentences.traditional: 後世史書對上官婉兒的生平進行了評述，
sentences.pinyin: hòu shì shǐ shū duì shàng guān wǎn ér de shēng píng jìn xíng le píng shù
sentences.english: The rebel army stormed the palace, and Shangguan Wan’er was killed.

sentences.simplified: 虽然肯定了其文学才能和对文化做出的贡献，但也因各种各样的原因，留下了一些污点性的描写。
sentences.traditional: 雖然肯定了其文學才能和對文化做出的貢獻，但也因各種各樣的原因，留下了一些污點性的描寫。
sentences.pinyin: suī rán kěn dìng le qí wén xué cái néng hé duì wén huà zuò chū de gòng xiàn dàn yě yīn gè zhǒng gè yàng de yuán yīn liú xià le yì xiē wū diǎn xìng de miáo xiě
sentences.english: Historical records of later generations commented on the life of Shangguan Wan’er.

sentences.simplified: 2013年，考古学家发现了上官婉儿的墓，
sentences.traditional: 2013年，考古學家發現了上官婉兒的墓，
sentences.pinyin: 4 nián kǎo gǔ xué jiā fā xiàn le shàng guān wǎn ér de mù
sentences.english: Although they affirmed her literary talent and cultural contributions, for various reasons, they also described some blemishes.

sentences.simplified: 墓碑上一篇900多字的墓志铭成为重要的考古材料。
sentences.traditional: 墓碑上一篇900多字的墓誌銘成為重要的考古材料。
sentences.pinyin: mù bēi shang yì piān 2 duō zì de mù zhì míng chéng wéi zhòng yào de kǎo gǔ cái liào
sentences.english: In 2013, archaeologists discovered the tomb of Shangguan Wan’er.

sentences.simplified: 墓志铭由武则天的女儿——也是红妆时代的另一位代表人物，太平公主所写。
sentences.traditional: 墓誌銘由武則天的女兒——也是紅妝時代的另一位代表人物，太平公主所寫。
sentences.pinyin: mù zhì míng yóu wǔ zé tiān de nǚ ér yě shì hóng zhuāng shí dài de lìng yí wèi dài biǎo rén wù tài píng gōng zhǔ suǒ xiě
sentences.english: The epitaph of over 900 characters on the tombstone became an important archaeological material.

sentences.simplified: 墓志铭书写了上官婉儿的一生，
sentences.traditional: 墓誌銘書寫了上官婉兒的一生，
sentences.pinyin: mù zhì míng shū xiě le shàng guān wǎn ér de yì shēng
sentences.english: The epitaph was written by Wu Zetian’s daughter, another representative figure of the “era of red makeup”, Princess Taiping.

sentences.simplified: 用极其优美和深刻的词汇赞美了上官婉儿的才华和品格。
sentences.traditional: 用極其優美和深刻的詞彙讚美了上官婉兒的才華和品格。
sentences.pinyin: yòng jí qí yōu měi hé shēn kè de cí huì zàn měi le shàng guān wǎn ér de cái huá hé pǐn gé
sentences.english: The epitaph narrates the life of Shangguan Wan’er.

sentences.simplified: 人们通过这篇墓志铭，认识了一个更全面的上官婉儿。
sentences.traditional: 人們通過這篇墓誌銘，認識了一個更全面的上官婉兒。
sentences.pinyin: rén men tōng guò zhè piān mù zhì míng rèn shi le yí ge gèng quán miàn de shàng guān wǎn ér
sentences.english: It uses extremely beautiful and profound words to praise Shangguan Wan’er’s talent and character.
Through this epitaph, people have gained a more complete understanding of Shangguan Wan’er.

sentences.simplified: 但不管是史书的评述，还是墓志铭的描写，
sentences.traditional: 但不管是史書的評述，還是墓誌銘的描寫，
sentences.pinyin: dàn bù guǎn shì shǐ shū de píng shù hái shi mù zhì míng de miáo xiě

sentences.simplified: 真实的上官婉儿是什么样的，也许我们很难完全了解。
sentences.traditional: 真實的上官婉兒是什麼樣的，也許我們很難完全了解。
sentences.pinyin: zhēn shí de shàng guān wǎn ér shì shén me yàng de yě xǔ wǒ men hěn nán wán quán liǎo jiě
sentences.english: But whether it’s the commentary in the historical records or the description in the epitaph, ..

sentences.simplified: 这正是历史的迷人之处，一个红妆时代的“巾帼宰相”，有着太多有意思的可能。
sentences.traditional: 這正是歷史的迷人之處，一個紅妝時代的“巾幗宰相”，有著太多有意思的可能。
sentences.pinyin: zhè zhèng shì lì shǐ de mí rén zhī chù yí ge hóng zhuāng shí dài de jīn guó zǎi xiàng yǒu zhe tài duō yǒu yì si de kě néng
sentences.english: .. perhaps we may never fully understand what the real Shangguan Wan’er was like.

sentence_translations: “Female Prime Minister”: Shangguan Wan’er
Wu Zetian of the Tang Dynasty was the only female emperor in Chinese history.
Her emergence was not only a historical first but also led the trend of women’s participation in politics.
In the eight or nine years after her abdication, several outstanding female politicians emerged one after another.
People call this unprecedented period in history the “era of red makeup”.
As Wu Zetian’s first assistant, Shangguan Wan’er was one of the important representative figures of the “era of red makeup”.
Shangguan Wan’er was born into a political family. Her grandfather was the prime minister.
But not long after her birth, her grandfather and father were killed by Wu Zetian, who was empress at the time, because they opposed her.
She and her mother were punished and sent to the palace to become low-ranking palace maids.
During her time as a palace maid, Shangguan Wan’er persisted in her studies and gained some fame due to her outstanding talent.
By the time Shangguan Wan’er was 13 years old, Wu Zetian heard that there was such an outstanding palace maid in the palace.
So, she called Shangguan Wan’er to see her. Wu Zetian asked many questions, and Shangguan Wan’er answered fluently.
Wu Zetian greatly valued talent.
Although Shangguan Wan’er’s grandfather and father had opposed her, Wu Zetian did not distrust Shangguan Wan’er because of this.
She expressed her sincerity to Shangguan Wan’er, inviting her to help govern the country.
Shangguan Wan’er was won over and put aside her own personal grievances.
She became Wu Zetian’s assistant, and from then on embarked on the path of politics.
For the next two decades and more, Shangguan Wan’er was always by Wu Zetian’s side.
She was highly valued by Wu Zetian, ..
.. expertly handling many major national affairs and fully demonstrating her personal wisdom and political talent.
She is referred to as the “female prime minister”, meaning that although she was a woman, ..
.. she could take on heavy responsibilities and participate in major national affairs just like a man.
After Wu Zetian abdicated, Shangguan Wan’er continued to gain the trust of the next emperor.
She still had the power to participate in decision-making for major national affairs.
In addition, she also persuaded the new emperor to establish academies, ..
.. providing a place for talented individuals to learn and showcase their abilities, ..
.. vigorously promoting cultural activities and cultivating a large number of outstanding talents for the country.
At the same time, she also wrote many beautiful poems and prose.
Not only was she admired by people, but she also became a model for poets across the country to learn from, ..
.. leaving behind a reputation as a “talented female scholar” in history.
Shangguan Wan’er’s life ended at the age of 47.
That year, the new emperor suddenly died of illness, and a coup occurred in the country.
The rebel army stormed the palace, and Shangguan Wan’er was killed.
Historical records of later generations commented on the life of Shangguan Wan’er.
Although they affirmed her literary talent and cultural contributions, for various reasons, they also described some blemishes.
In 2013, archaeologists discovered the tomb of Shangguan Wan’er.
The epitaph of over 900 characters on the tombstone became an important archaeological material.
The epitaph was written by Wu Zetian’s daughter, another representative figure of the “era of red makeup”, Princess Taiping.
The epitaph narrates the life of Shangguan Wan’er.
It uses extremely beautiful and profound words to praise Shangguan Wan’er’s talent and character.
Through this epitaph, people have gained a more complete understanding of Shangguan Wan’er.
But whether it’s the commentary in the historical records or the description in the epitaph, ..
.. perhaps we may never fully understand what the real Shangguan Wan’er was like.
This is precisely the charm of history. A “female prime minister” of the “era of red makeup” has so many interesting possibilities.
